ei.title: Chapter 5-15: The Country-of-Origin Effect on Consumers
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Knowledge about a product's country of origin can affect the way consumers think about it. Just as we stereotype people based on where they were born, we stereotype products based on where they were made. Consumers in developing countries, for instance, often infer higher quality for brands perceived as foreign. Conversely, consumers in some nations believe their country's products are superior to those made elsewhere. Japanese consumers, for example, tend to infer that made-in-Japan products are higher quality than made-in-America products. Therefore, a luggage company markets its pricier luggage in Japan by stressing that the products are designed and made in Japan. Consumers are more likely to make inferences about a brand based on its country of origin when they are unmotivated to process brand information or when their processing goal guides attention towards origin information. If consumers dislike a country's political or social policies, they may respond negatively to its products.

Therefore, a luggage company markets its pricier luggage in Japan by stressing that the products are designed and made in Japan. questions.passage: Knowledge about a product's country of origin can ①<u>affect</u> the way consumers think about it. Just as we stereotype people based on where they were born, we stereotype products based on where they were made. Consumers in developing countries, for instance, often infer higher quality for brands perceived as ②<u>domestic</u>. Conversely, consumers in some nations believe their country's products are ③<u>superior</u> to those made elsewhere. Japanese consumers, for example, tend to infer that made-in-Japan products are higher quality than made-in-America products. Therefore, a luggage company markets its pricier luggage in Japan by stressing that the products are designed and made in Japan. Consumers are more likely to make inferences about a brand based on its country of origin when they are unmotivated to process brand information or when their processing goal guides attention towards origin information. If consumers ④<u>dislike</u> a country's political or social policies, they may respond negatively to its products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 개발 도상국 소비자는 외국산(foreign) 브랜드에 더 높은 품질을 추단하므로 국내의(domestic)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>affect</u> (영향을 미치다) — 원산지 지식이 사고에 영향을 미친다, 적절

② <u>domestic</u> (국내의) — 원문 foreign(외국의). 개발 도상국 소비자는 외국산 브랜드를 더 높이 평가하므로 domestic 부적절 ←정답

③ <u>superior</u> (우수한) — 자국 제품이 더 우수하다고 믿는다, 적절

④ <u>dislike</u> (싫어하다) — 정책을 싫어하면 제품에 부정적 반응, 적절

questions.passage: Knowledge about a product's country of origin can affect the way consumers think about it. Just as we stereotype people based on where they were ①<u>born</u>, we stereotype products based on where they were made. Consumers in ②<u>developing</u> countries, for instance, often infer higher quality for brands perceived as foreign. Conversely, consumers in some nations believe their country's products are ③<u>inferior</u> to those made elsewhere. Japanese consumers, for example, tend to infer that made-in-Japan products are higher quality than made-in-America products. Therefore, a luggage company markets its pricier luggage in Japan by stressing that the products are designed and made in Japan. Consumers are more likely to make inferences about a brand based on its country of origin when they are unmotivated to process brand information or when their processing goal guides attention towards origin information. If consumers dislike a country's political or social policies, they may respond ④<u>negatively</u> to its products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 일부 국가 소비자는 자국 제품이 더 우수하다(superior)고 믿으므로 열등하다(inferior)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>born</u> (태어난) — 사람을 태어난 곳으로 고정관념화, 적절

② <u>developing</u> (개발 도상의) — 개발 도상국 소비자, 적절

③ <u>inferior</u> (열등한) — 원문 superior(우수한). 자국 제품이 더 우수하다고 믿는 맥락에서 inferior 부적절 ←정답

④ <u>negatively</u> (부정적으로) — 정책이 싫으면 부정적으로 반응, 적절

questions.passage: Knowledge about a product's country of origin can affect the way consumers think about it. Just as we stereotype people based on where they were born, we stereotype products based on where they were made. Consumers in developing countries, for instance, often ①<u>infer lower quality</u> for brands perceived as foreign. Conversely, consumers in some nations believe their country's products are superior to those made elsewhere. Japanese consumers, for example, ②<u>tend</u> to infer that made-in-Japan products are higher quality than made-in-America products. Therefore, a luggage company markets its pricier luggage in Japan by stressing that the products are ③<u>designed</u> and made in Japan. Consumers are more likely to make inferences about a brand based on its country of origin when they are unmotivated to process brand information or when their processing goal guides attention towards origin information. If consumers dislike a country's political or social policies, they may ④<u>respond</u> negatively to its products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 개발 도상국 소비자는 외국산 브랜드에 더 높은 품질(higher quality)을 추단하므로 lower quality는 부적절.
det.analysis:
① <u>infer lower quality</u> (더 낮은 품질을 추단) — 원문 infer higher quality. 개발 도상국 소비자는 외국산에 더 높은 품질을 추단하므로 lower 부적절 ←정답

② <u>tend</u> (경향이 있다) — 일본 소비자가 추단하는 경향, 적절

③ <u>designed</u> (디자인된) — 일본에서 디자인되고 만들어진, 적절

④ <u>respond</u> (반응하다) — 제품에 부정적으로 반응, 적절
det.tip: infer higher quality(더 높은 품질을 추단) ↔ infer lower quality

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

questions.passage: Knowledge about a product's country of origin can affect the way consumers think about it. Just as we stereotype people based on where they were born, we __________. Consumers in developing countries, for instance, often infer higher quality for brands perceived as foreign. Conversely, consumers in some nations believe their country's products are superior to those made elsewhere. Japanese consumers, for example, tend to infer that made-in-Japan products are higher quality than made-in-America products. Therefore, a luggage company markets its pricier luggage in Japan by stressing that the products are designed and made in Japan. Consumers are more likely to make inferences about a brand based on its country of origin when they are unmotivated to process brand information or when their processing goal guides attention towards origin information. If consumers dislike a country's political or social policies, they may respond negatively to its products.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람을 태어난 곳으로 판단하듯, '제품도 만들어진 곳에 근거해 고정관념화한다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① stereotype products based on where they were made (제품을 만들어진 곳으로 고정관념화) — 사람↔제품의 병렬 구조 ←정답
❌ ② judge people only by their personality (성격으로만 판단) — 원산지 주제와 무관
❌ ③ ignore the origin of all the products (원산지를 무시) — 반대
❌ ④ buy products regardless of their price (가격과 무관하게 구매) — 무관
det.tip: Just as we A, we B = 우리가 A하듯 B한다 (병렬)
